title: NVME Identify Controller: decode all fields up to 256 bytes
description:
This is to resolve reported issue #17282.

This will be a work in-progress, the first merge request provides full decoding of the first 256 bytes. Attached files show the dissector enhancement.

![image](/uploads/33b9dbcc88aeb016a4c84273ecf0c6c8/image.png)
![image](/uploads/59ec039b7ce755bdd3a29c4931516e72/image.png)

Hi, IMHO this way of coding renders the code prety much unreadable. I prefere 
    proto_tree_add_item(cmd_tree, hf_nvme_identify_ctrl_vid, cmd_tvb,
                        0, 2, ENC_LITTLE_ENDIAN);
With the fixed zero replaced by offset and the offset increased as needed.

@AndersBroman, thank you for the reply.

So, when we add the description of the field (name, decoding type, mask), it is done in a structured way:

```
{ &hf_nvme_identify_ctrl_vid,
            { "PCI Vendor ID (VID)", "nvme.cmd.identify.ctrl.vid",
               FT_UINT16, BASE_HEX, NULL, 0x0, NULL, HFILL}
        },
```

and basically this specifies how the field will be displayed.

While the following --
```
proto_tree_add_item(cmd_tree, hf_nvme_identify_ctrl_vid, cmd_tvb,
                        0, 2, ENC_LITTLE_ENDIAN);
```
only really specifies the offset and size.

With so many entries per page (and some GetLog Pages are 3 pages), it becomes really cumbersome to add the code (especially with the coding styled of 2-3 lines per entry), and even more so to read it. I got tired...

Another issue is group entries and group mask entries -- a lot of code would also be repeated.

I do not believe I have removed something from the readability of the code -- we still have  one entry per line, that specifies offset and size, for example:
```
{ .type = TREE_ENT_REGULAR, .field = hf_nvme_identify_ctrl_vid, .dec_type = ENC_LITTLE_ENDIAN, .offset = 0, .bytes = 2 },
```


What is really simplified though, is adding and decoding groups, and in the end analysis for the entire page decoding, it improves readability.

Also, 
`.type = TREE_ENT_REGULAR, .dec_type = ENC_LITTLE_ENDIAN` can be considered default, and then most entries would become as follows:

```
{ .field = hf_nvme_identify_ctrl_vid, .offset = 0, .bytes = 2 },
```

Is it not simpler?

Can you please reconsider and approve? Another opinion perhaps?

+1 with Anders, it is may be more easy for you but all other dissector use this format

you can look also may be ptv stuff
@alagoutte, "you can look also may be ptv stuff" -- what did you mean by that? Do you refer to code?

there is a ptv_cursor (look on source) i can be help

for bitmask, there is proto_tree_add_bitmask for help

I have looked at the use of proto_tree_add_bitmask() -- it does not help much.
To use that, I would have to write many array declarations, and this would result it twice more code for each item.

I rather prefer the approach quoted above -- define array to start with, and iterate in a loop.

Regarding  ptv_cursor, I could not find anything. Looks like a wrong name. I have tried various spelling variations -- no luck. Not sure what you meant.

@alagoutte,@AndersBroman, I have reworked the code per your review comments.

Can you please approve it now?
